title: Book One · Chapter 155: A Word in Two Parts
story:
Ronan cannot read one word on the stool card quickly. He wrote it from Dad's paper, so the letters are right. He still stops in the middle of it.

“Repaired,” Mei says.

“I know.”

“Then why are you angry at it?”

Ronan looks at the word again. His face looks angry. Mei noticed his face. He puts the card down.

“I want to say it right when people come.”

They are in the classroom after lunch. Leo is outside with the ball. Mei is waiting for paint to dry. She has ten minutes, not the whole afternoon.

She covers the end of the word with her thumb. Ronan reads the first part. Then she shows the rest. He says it again, more slowly. He does not try to say it quickly this time. Now he can say all of it.

“Now the whole line,” she says.

He reads: DAD REPAIRED IT. He can do that. Then he reads from the start. He stops at the same word again.

Mei gives him the card. “Again after a rest.”

“Can we do it now?”

“I have my own words to check.”

He nods. She gets her drawing list. One street name has a letter she always turns the wrong way. Ronan knows that one. He points it out only after she asks him to look.

They work quietly at the same desk. He reads his three lines under his breath. She writes the name once on a separate sheet. Neither is teaching the other everything. Ronan can help Mei with a letter. Mei can help Ronan with a word.

At break Ronan goes outside. Leo throws the ball too high. It hits the wall and comes back towards Mei's window. Ronan catches it before it reaches the glass.

“A very good repair,” he calls.

“Nothing broke,” Leo says.

“A very early repair.”

They laugh. Ronan said the word himself. He did not look at the card. That surprises him. He was only thinking about the ball.

At home Dad reads the card with him. He says the word once, then lets Ronan try the whole line. They sit beside the real stool and read together. Ronan points at the leg as he speaks.

“What if I forget?” he asks.

“You can read it. Or say I fixed it.”

“Is that cheating?”

Dad looks at the stool. “It would be the same stool.”

Ronan smiles. Visitors need to understand the repair. Ronan can use simple words and tell them. One wrong sound will not change the repaired stool. He still practises twice more. Then he puts the card away.

Before Dad goes outside, Ronan asks him to listen again. “Please wait when I stop,” Ronan says. “Let me try again myself.” Dad does. There is a small silence in the middle, but Ronan gets through it. He puts a finger under the last line and finishes. Dad smiles only when Ronan has finished speaking. Ronan sees the smile after his last line. Dad waited and listened to all of it.

After supper he opens his school reading book. There is another hard word on the next page. He does not ask Dad to make every word easy. He tries the first part, then the second. He reads the whole line again. Does it make sense now?

He gets it almost right. Mum helps with the last sound. Ronan reads the page again before bed. The story moves forward this time. What will the boys do next? He wants to read on. He puts a strip of paper beside the next page. He can start there tomorrow.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：repaired / fixed＝修好了；under his breath＝小声地；sense＝意思。

情节提示：thumb＝拇指；silence＝安静、停顿；cheating＝作弊、耍花招。

理解：1. Mei 怎样帮助 Ronan 读这个词？2. Dad 为什么认为换成“fixed”也可以？
